 WASHINGTON (TNND) — Voters across the country are casting ballots in midterm elections to determine control of Congress, statehouses and governorships with a chance to shake up the balance of power in Washington and beyond amid rising frustrations over high prices and the war with Iran.
 Democrats are hoping to capitalize on those frustrations and came into Election Day with polls showing the party making gains in states and districts that have tilted toward Republicans in recent cycles. The Democrats only need to net three more seats to take back the House, while they need to gain four seats to win the Senate.
 Polling places started closing at 6 p.m. Eastern and cascade throughout the night, with the final polls closing at 1 a.m. Eastern in Alaska. How quickly ballots are counted varies from state to state, creating an uncertain timeline for races to be called on Election Night depending on rules over counting and how close elections end up being. In tight races, results may not be known for days or even weeks as officials count ballots.
 Follow live coverage as votes are counted and control of government takes shape (All times Eastern):
 8:20 P.M.: CHRIS PAPPAS WINS NEW HAMPSHIRE SENATE RACE 
 Democrat Chris Pappas defeated former Sen. John Sununu in a closely watched Senate race that was one of Republicans' best pickup opportunities this cycle.
 8:13 P.M.: DEMOCRATS HANG ONTO REDRAWN DISTRICTS 
 Democrats won two districts that Republicans in Florida redrew ahead of this year’s midterms with wins by Reps. Jared Moskowitz and Kathy Castor in districts that were remade to be more favorable for Republicans.
 In Florida’s 25th District that now stretches from South Beach to Delray Beach, Moskowitz defeated former Boca Raton Mayor Scott Singer, who was backed by Trump.
 Castor won in the newly redrawn 14th Congressional District, which would have backed the GOP by double-digits in the 2024 election.
 7:55 P.M. JON OSSOFF WINS REELECTION IN GEORGIA 
 Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection in Georgia, defeating Republican Rep. Mike Collins in a key battleground to determine control of the Senate.
 Ossoff was one of the GOP's potential flip chances representing a state that backed Trump in the 2024 election, but held strong leads in polling and fundraising throughout the race. 
 7:30 P.M.: VOTING ENDS IN MORE STATES 
 Polls in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia have closed for the evening. In North Carolina and Ohio, there are tight Senate races that will be crucial to determining control of the chamber for the next two years. Ohio's gubernatorial race between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, is also being closely watched as a potential flip in a heavily Republican-leaning state. 
 Democratic former Gov. Roy Cooper is favored to flip North Carolina's Senate seat being vacated by the retirement of Republican Sen. Thom Tillis. Michael Whatley, the former chair of the Republican National Committee, has trailed in polling running up to Election Day.
 7 P.M.: FIRST RACES CALLED AS MORE STATES CLOSE POLLS 
 Race calls are starting as more polls close across the country. 
 In Kentucky, Republican Rep. Hal Rogers won reelection to the state's 5th Congressional District and Democrat Morgan McGarvey was reelected in the 3rd Congressional District.
 Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., also won reelection.
 Voting is now closed in Indiana, Kentucky, Virginia, Vermont, South Carolina and Georgia. Some polling stations have also started to close in New Hampshire and Florida.
 6 P.M.: POLLS START TO CLOSE 
 Polls in a handful of districts in Kentucky and Indiana have closed, the first of the evening. Other states on the East Coast will start closing polling stations at 7 p.m.
